connectionPool.title: HikariCP Connection Pool Mechanics & Exhaustion
connectionPool.subtitle: Visualize thread connection borrowing, active connection leasing, pool boundary limits, and request thread waiting queues during load bursts.
connectionPool.mentalModel: HikariCP maintains pre-allocated DB connections in a pool; threads borrow connections for queries and return them immediately — pool exhaustion causes request queuing and timeouts.

failureModes: Connection Leak: Forgetting to close a connection or keeping long-running non-DB operations inside a transactional method holds the pooled connection hostage until pool exhaustion.
Pool Starvation: Configuring pool max-size lower than peak concurrent HTTP worker threads causes `SQLTransientConnectionException: Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms`.
tradeOffs: Fixed Pool Size vs Dynamic Sizing: HikariCP recommends a FIXED pool size (`maximumPoolSize == minimumIdle`) to eliminate latency spikes caused by on-demand connection creation.
theoryData.productionScenario: An API Gateway crashed under peak load with 30-second HTTP timeouts. Diagnostics showed HikariCP pool size was set to 10 connections for 200 Tomcat worker threads. Tuning pool size to `(CPU cores * 2) + effective_spindle_count` = 32 and setting `leakDetectionThreshold=2000ms` resolved the bottleneck.

interviewQA.q: Why is HikariCP significantly faster than legacy connection pools like C3P0 or DBCP?
interviewQA.a: HikariCP uses bytecode optimization, FastList (custom ArrayList replacement without range-checks), ConcurrentBag lock-free borrowing using ThreadLocal thread-level connection caching, and eliminates synchronized overhead.

quizData.question: What happens when all connections in a HikariCP pool are in use and a new request thread arrives?
quizData.answer: The new thread enters a FIFO waiting queue and blocks until an active connection is returned or until `connectionTimeout` (default 30s) expires, throwing `SQLTransientConnectionException`.
